content.text:
**No — not as a tool you can just add.** LinkedIn has no public, self-serve “post this job” API. Direct posting is a closed Talent Solutions partner product, and Kuchup’s current wrapping is the only path that actually works without that partnership.

## What you have today

Kuchup does not push jobs to LinkedIn. It publishes public `/jobs/<slug>` pages with `schema.org/JobPosting` JSON-LD, LinkedInBot crawls them, and they show up as **Basic Jobs** on the Kuchup company page. Apply lands on Kuchup, not the employer ATS. That is documented in `docs/reference/job-syndication.md`.

LinkedIn’s own product called **Job Wrapping** is different: Recruiter customers ingest jobs from *their* ATS/career site into *their* paid job slots. You are using crawler wrapping as a job board, not Recruiter wrapping.

## What “post directly” actually is

There are three official push channels. All are partner-gated:

| Channel | What it does | Can Kuchup just build it? |
|---|---|---|
| **Job Posting API** (`/simpleJobPostings`) | Push Basic or paid jobs on behalf of a Recruiter customer | No. LinkedIn says they are **not accepting new Job Posting API partnerships**. Access requires a signed API agreement, parent/child app provisioning, certification, and usually an onboarding widget for the employer’s `companyId` / `contractId`. |
| **Apply Connect** | Same API family, plus Easy Apply and application webhooks. This is the path they now point new partners to. | Same gate. Aimed at ATS products posting *for their customers* (Greenhouse, Lever, etc.). |
| **XML feed** | LinkedIn periodically pulls a partner feed and creates Basic Jobs | Also partner-gated. Request goes through LinkedIn BD (`LL-BD@linkedin.com`), then they review the feed. Not an API you call from a button. |

A Community Management / “share this as a company post” integration is not a substitute. Those are feed posts, not Jobs-tab listings, and blasting other companies’ roles as organic posts is a ToS problem.

## The harder issue than the API

Even with a partner key, the API is built for **employers (or their ATS) posting their own jobs**. You would need each real employer’s LinkedIn company ID, and often a Recruiter contract, plus they must accept LinkedIn’s Jobs terms.

Kuchup’s catalog is other companies’ visa roles, with `hiringOrganization` set to Kuchup so LinkedIn attaches them to *your* page. Pushing that through the API would be the same attribution, just more explicit. LinkedIn already treats staffing / search / generic-name jobs as abuse-prone and often **requires paid promotion** or drops them from Basic Jobs.

So a “post to LinkedIn” MCP/panel tool would not give you:

- jobs attributed to FlixBus / Stripe / whoever
- guaranteed Jobs-search distribution
- control over crawl lag

It would give you a partner sales process, certification, and a high chance they classify you as a job board/aggregator and say no — or only allow paid slots under the Kuchup page.

## Practical recommendation

Stay on wrapping. It is the only channel that matches the product (aggregate visa roles → capture apply on Kuchup). Make wrapping more reliable instead of replacing it: stable slugs, 410 on close, sitemap, JSON-LD, logo, consistent `hiringOrganization`.

If distribution is still too slow or incomplete, the next *real* step is a BD conversation for an **XML feed as a job board**, not building an API client. Expect them to ask who the hiring company is and why apply does not go to the employer.

Do not scrape Recruiter, fake Job Posting API calls, or auto-post listings as company updates. That is the path that gets the company page restricted.

If you want, we can next compare wrapping vs XML feed vs paid Recruiter slots against the actual funnel (LinkedIn Apply → `/jobs/<slug>/save` → workspace), and what would break if LinkedIn started attributing jobs to the real employer instead of Kuchup.

You do have options. What you don’t have is a public LinkedIn API you can wire into Kuchup this week.

**You cannot** add a tool that `POST`s jobs to LinkedIn like you would to your own backend. That endpoint is partner-only, and they are not onboarding new Job Posting API apps.

**You can** still get jobs onto LinkedIn as real listings. The paths are commercial, not a coding task.

## What actually works

**1. Pay for LinkedIn job slots (most direct)**  
Buy Recruiter / job slots for the Kuchup company page. Then you post from LinkedIn’s own UI, or point Recruiter Job Wrapping at `kuchup.com/jobs`. That *is* posting onto LinkedIn, with guaranteed inventory, close/renew, and Apply URL control. Cost is the product (typically thousands/year), not engineering.

Same product constraint as wrapping: listings sit on **Kuchup’s** page, not FlixBus/Stripe. LinkedIn also often forces staffing/aggregator-style jobs onto **paid** slots and drops them from free Basic Jobs. For your catalog, paid slots may be the only way they stay up.

**2. Apply as a job-board partner (XML / Apply Connect)**  
Email LinkedIn Talent BD and ask to send an XML feed (or Apply Connect). If they say yes, jobs sync on a schedule. If they say no, that’s usually because you are aggregating other employers’ roles and capturing apply. Timeline is weeks–months, not a sprint.

**3. Use a distributor that already has LinkedIn**  
Broadbean, Jobtarget, eQuest, Appcast, and similar already hold the partnership. You send them a feed; they post to LinkedIn. You pay per job or per contract. This is how most non-ATS companies “post directly” without becoming a LinkedIn partner.

**4. Keep crawler wrapping**  
This is the free path you already built. It is real LinkedIn Jobs inventory when LinkedInBot picks a page up. It is just slow, incomplete, and not something you trigger with a button.

Organic company-page posts (“visa role at X, apply on Kuchup”) can drive clicks. They are **not** Jobs search listings.

## What this means for Kuchup

If the goal is “a tool in the app that publishes a catalog row to LinkedIn on demand,” that tool does not exist unless you first have (2) or (3), or you buy (1) and post through LinkedIn’s product.

The realistic split:

| Goal | Path |
|---|---|
| Reliable listings on LinkedIn now | Paid job slots or a distributor |
| Official push API / XML | BD partnership, maybe never |
| Zero extra cost | Current wrapping |

So you are not stuck with “LinkedIn is impossible.” You are stuck with “LinkedIn will not let a random app post jobs for free.” Wrapping is the free hack; paid slots or a distributor is the actual posting product.

LinkedIn does not publish a price list. Buyer-reported 2026 numbers, and they scale with **how many jobs are live at once**, not with “I have a catalog.”

## What you would actually pay

| Path | Cost | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Current wrapping | **$0** | Basic Jobs if LinkedInBot crawls `/jobs/<slug>` |
| One free LinkedIn post | **$0** | One listing, ~14 days, weak reach. Aggregator/staffing-style jobs often get blocked or forced to paid. |
| Promoted job (self-serve) | **~$7–10/day minimum** → **~$210–300/month per job** | Auction PPC. Competitive eng roles often need **$500+/month** to show. |
| Job slot (sales contract) | **~$200–450/slot/month** typical; **$150–350** in much of EU; up to **$1,000** for senior US tech | One always-on listing you can swap. Usually 6–12 month contract. |
| Recruiter Lite | **~$170/month** | Sourcing/InMail. **Does not** include slots. One free post per seat in some plans. |
| Recruiter Corporate | **~$10k+/seat/year**, often 3-seat minimum | Slots are an add-on, not included. |

A distributor (Broadbean, Jobtarget, etc.) still charges LinkedIn’s board cost **plus** their license. It is not a cheap workaround.

## The number that matters for Kuchup

Paid LinkedIn is priced **per concurrent listing**. Wrapping can put hundreds of visa roles on the Kuchup page for free. Buying that same inventory is a different product.

Rough math if you promoted or slotted every live visa role:

- **10 jobs** promoted at the floor: **~$2k–3k/month**
- **50 jobs** in slots at $250: **~$12.5k/month** (~$150k/year)
- **200 jobs**: **tens of thousands per month**

That is why wrapping exists. LinkedIn will not sell you a board’s worth of listings at consumer prices.

## What is realistic

If the goal is “some jobs reliably on LinkedIn, Apply still hits Kuchup”:

- **Pilot:** 1 promoted post for 2 weeks → about **$150–300**, see if apply traffic is even worth it.
- **Small paid inventory:** 3–5 EU slots → about **$600–2,000/month**, rotate the best visa roles.
- **Whole catalog:** wrapping, or a partner XML feed if BD ever says yes. Paying per job does not scale.

Recruiter seats are a separate bill. You only need them if you also want to search/message people. Posting alone is Promoted Jobs or slots.

LinkedIn sales quotes vary by country mix (UK/DE/NL vs US) and whether they treat Kuchup as a staffing/job board. Expect them to push paid slots and to refuse free Basic posts for aggregated third-party roles.

**A few days if LinkedIn already knows the page. Often longer. Not guaranteed for every job.**

You are not on Recruiter Job Wrapping (that refreshes at least every 24 hours). You are waiting for LinkedInBot to find public HTML and turn it into a Basic Job. That is a batch crawl, not a webhook.

## Realistic wait

| Situation | Typical time to show on LinkedIn |
|---|---|
| Recruiter wrapping / partner XML (you don’t have this) | ~6–24 hours after they already ingest you |
| Organic crawl of a **known** careers URL | **~1–3 days** median; a long tail of **~5–10 days** |
| New `/jobs/<slug>` URL they have never seen | **Days to weeks**, sometimes **never** |
| Close / 410 after they already wrapped it | Next recrawl, often **1–2 days**, can lag longer |

Industry crawls of employer career sites (no paid feed) sit around **2.8 days median**. Partner XML is faster because LinkedIn hits a known feed on a schedule (job boards about every 24 hours). Kuchup is the slower path.

Your own SEO notes already treat individual job URLs as **days–weeks**, not hours. That matches this.

## What “wait” does not mean

It does not mean the whole visa catalog appears. LinkedIn already wrapped a **few strings from country marketing pages**. That only proves they crawl kuchup.com sometimes. It does not mean they will walk `/sitemap-jobs.xml` and post every slug.

`/sitemap-jobs.xml` is mainly for Google. LinkedInBot usually follows links from pages it already has (homepage, country pages, jobs it wrapped before). A new slug with no inbound link can sit unpublished.

They also skip jobs: staffing/aggregator-style listings, generic hiring orgs, incomplete schema, duplicates of the real employer’s own LinkedIn post. Kuchup’s `hiringOrganization = Kuchup` plus a third-party employer in the title is exactly the kind of listing they may ingest slowly, drop, or never promote.

Catalog roles also turn over every fetch. A job can close on the ATS before LinkedIn wraps it.

## How to tell if a given job landed

Search LinkedIn Jobs for the title + Kuchup, or check the Kuchup company page Jobs tab. There is no dashboard for unpaid Basic Jobs unless you have Recruiter.

**Practical expectation:** some roles in **2–7 days** after the URL is live and linked from a page they already crawl; do not plan on same-day, and do not assume full coverage.

content.text:
LinkedIn’s docs are clear on one point: **you cannot ping LinkedInBot.** There is no Indexing API, no “request crawl,” no sitemap that forces a recrawl. Speed comes from changing *how* they ingest, or from making pages so easy to find and so complete that the next crawl actually posts them instead of skipping them.

## What the docs say is actually faster

LinkedIn treats three methods as different clocks ([automated job posts FAQ](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a453826), [XML FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds-faq?view=li-lts-2026-03)):

| Method | Clock they document | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| Job Posting API | Near real time | Partner only; they are not taking new apps |
| XML feed | ATS every **6 hours**, job boards every **24 hours** | Email `LL-BD@linkedin.com` with listing volume, markets, search URL, sample job URLs. Host a **full** feed at a stable URL, refresh at least every **12 hours** |
| Recruiter Job Wrapping | At least every **24 hours**, often more | Buy slots, then set **Job source URL** to your careers/jobs page or a LinkedIn-format XML |
| Organic scrape of HTML | Unscheduled | What you have now |

So the documented way to go from “days–weeks / maybe never” to “next day” is **XML or Recruiter wrapping**, not better JSON-LD.

XML is free to ingest once they accept you ([FAQ: they do not charge for Basic Jobs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds-faq?view=li-lts-2026-03)). The wait is BD + certification (they say feed work is often **2–8 weeks**), not the scrape interval.

## What you can do without a partnership

These do not make the crawler faster. They make the *next* visit more likely to discover and accept the job.

**1. Put job URLs on pages they already crawl**  
They wrapped country marketing pages. The Next homepage currently has **no `/jobs/…` links**. A crawler that only has `/relocation-jobs-germany` will not invent slugs. LinkedIn wrapping setup even asks for a **job source URL** (a list/careers page), not a sitemap ([set up automated job postings](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a1306845/set-up-automated-job-postings)).

Practically: an HTML jobs index (or country pages that list live visa URLs), linked from the homepage, country pages, footer, and the LinkedIn company page website field. Server-rendered, no login, no JS-only list.

**2. Keep Apply on a stable, non-redirecting HTTPS URL**  
XML guide: no redirecting job URLs; `applyUrl` should be where the person actually starts apply. You already keep Apply on `/jobs/<slug>` (good). Don’t 302 LinkedIn traffic.

**3. Make listings “complete” so they don’t get dropped**  
From the [XML FAQ / development guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds-development-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03):

- Description **≥ 100 characters** (thin JD pages get skipped)
- Location as **city + country/region**, not city alone (`London, United Kingdom`)
- Full open set only — drop closed jobs (you already 410 + drop from sitemap)
- Don’t churn the same role closed/reopened
- Workplace: `#LI-Onsite` / `#LI-Hybrid` / `#LI-Remote` in the description (they say hashtags win over a field)

**4. Put the company page URL on the LinkedIn Page**  
`sameAs` / logo / a public jobs hub URL on the Page help mapping. You already set `hiringOrganization` to Kuchup + `/logo.png`.

**5. File a Jobs ticket only if they already ingest you**  
[XML FAQ support flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds-faq?view=li-lts-2026-03): Help Center → Other → Jobs. That is for “opt in this employer / this feed,” not “please crawl my new HTML.” Without Recruiter or a feed they already scrape, it usually goes nowhere.

Google Indexing API / Search Console **do not** notify LinkedIn.

## The catch in LinkedIn’s own rules

Their feed guide also says:

- Jobs must be tied to the **real employer**, not the job board
- Do **not** put your company name in place of the hiring company
- **Exclude jobs aggregated from other sites**; Apply should go to where the application is completed

Your current JSON-LD does the opposite on purpose (`hiringOrganization: Kuchup`, Apply stays on Kuchup). That is why some listings may never go live even after a crawl: staffing/generic-name jobs often **must be promoted** ([same FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds-faq?view=li-lts-2026-03)).

So “faster” and “all jobs on the Kuchup Page” fight each other. Correct-per-docs markup would map to FlixBus/Mollie and send Apply to the ATS. Your funnel wants the opposite.

## What I would do, in order

1. **HTML job index + links from country pages** — cheapest discovery fix; matches how they already found you.
2. **Richer location + 100+ char descriptions + workplace hashtags** — fewer silent skips.
3. **Email `LL-BD@linkedin.com`** with volume, markets, a search/list URL, and sample `/jobs/<slug>` URLs — that is the documented 24-hour path.
4. If BD says no, **a few Recruiter slots** pointed at that same job-source URL — documented 24-hour wrapping.

You cannot make unpaid HTML wrapping as fast as a feed. You can only get discovered sooner and rejected less often.

# Faster LinkedIn job wrapping

## Recommendation

Do **not** buy job slots for the visa catalog, and do **not** wait on the Job Posting API (closed to new partners).

Best sequence:

1. **Ship a public jobs hub now** so LinkedInBot can walk from country/homepage pages it already crawled to every `/jobs/<slug>`. Today there is no HTML list; `/sitemap-jobs.xml` is a Google sitemap, not a LinkedIn job source.
2. **Expose a LinkedIn-format XML feed** at a stable URL and email Talent BD. Once they accept it, their docs say job-board feeds are scraped **every 24 hours** (ATS feeds every 6 hours). That is the real speed upgrade.
3. **Keep Apply on Kuchup** (`https://kuchup.com/jobs/<slug>`). Do not send Apply to the employer ATS. `hiringOrganization` stays Kuchup so listings still map to the Kuchup Page.

BD may still refuse the feed because LinkedIn’s XML guide wants the **real employer** and excludes jobs aggregated from other sites. If they say no, the hub still helps organic wrapping; paid slots remain a later, small-inventory option (3–5 roles), not a catalog strategy.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  CountryPages["Country marketing pages"] --> JobsHub
  Homepage["Homepage / footer"] --> JobsHub
  JobsHub["GET /jobs"] --> JobPage["GET /jobs/slug"]
  XmlFeed["GET /feeds/linkedin-jobs.xml"] --> LinkedInBD["LinkedIn scrape if BD accepts"]
  JobPage --> LinkedInBot["LinkedInBot organic"]
  LinkedInBot --> BasicJobs["Kuchup Basic Jobs"]
  LinkedInBD --> BasicJobs
```

## Phase 1 — Crawlable job source URL

Flask SSR, same reason as job detail pages: the list changes every fetch and must not live in the Next static export.

- New `GET /jobs` in [`relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py`](relocation_jobs/web/routes/job_pages.py), registered as a distinct route from `/jobs/<slug>` (Flask allows both; catch-all `/<path:slug>` in [`relocation_jobs/web/server.py`](relocation_jobs/web/server.py) already loses to explicit routes).
- New repo query next to [`list_active_public_job_sitemap_entries`](relocation_jobs/catalog/repo.py): visa-positive, open, slug present, with title / company / country / location — reused by the hub and the XML feed.
- Template + [`job-posting.css`](relocation_jobs/static/job-posting.css): grouped by country, each row a real `<a href="/jobs/{slug}">`. Optional `?country=uk` filter. No login wall, JSON-LD `ItemList` optional.
- Cache like job pages: `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=86400`.
- Add `/jobs` to Flask [`/sitemap.xml`](relocation_jobs/web/server.py) (marketing sitemap), **not** to `/sitemap-jobs.xml`.
- Add `/jobs` to [`tests/helpers/route_manifest.py`](tests/helpers/route_manifest.py).

Inbound links from pages LinkedIn already saw:

- Footer + hero note in [`homepage/components/Footer.tsx`](homepage/components/Footer.tsx) and [`homepage/components/Hero.tsx`](homepage/components/Hero.tsx) → `/jobs`.
- Each country marketing page ([`homepage/app/[slug]/page.tsx`](homepage/app/[slug]/page.tsx)) → `/jobs?country={key}` (static href; no Postgres in Next).
- After homepage export/deploy, set the LinkedIn company Page website / custom button to `https://kuchup.com/jobs` (ops, not code).

## Phase 2 — Fewer silent skips when they do crawl

Small JSON-LD / copy fixes in [`relocation_jobs/catalog/service.py`](relocation_jobs/catalog/service.py) `job_posting_json_ld` and the job page body:

- Location as city **and** country/region (`London, United Kingdom`), not city alone.
- Description floor: keep the existing Kuchup note so listings stay ≥100 characters (LinkedIn XML minimum).
- Workplace hashtags in the description when known (`#LI-Onsite` / `#LI-Hybrid` / `#LI-Remote`); skip if the catalog has no workplace field.
- Do **not** change `hiringOrganization` to the real employer (that would map jobs off the Kuchup Page).

## Phase 3 — LinkedIn XML feed (BD-ready)

New `GET /feeds/linkedin-jobs.xml` (avoid `/jobs/<slug>` capturing a filename). Same open visa set as the hub. Full snapshot on each GET (LinkedIn requires a **complete** list, not a delta). Recommend regenerating at least every 12 hours — on-request from Postgres matches the sitemap.

Shape per [XML development guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/xml-feeds-development-guide?view=li-lts-2026-03):

- `partnerJobId` = catalog `id` (≤40 chars)
- `company` = `Kuchup`
- `companyId` / `posterEmail` from env (`LINKEDIN_COMPANY_ID`, `LINKEDIN_JOB_POSTER_EMAIL`) — placeholders in docs, real values only in gitignored `.env`
- `title` = catalog title (XML titles are frozen once posted; do not churn)
- `description` = HTML in CDATA (supported tags only)
- `applyUrl` = `https://kuchup.com/jobs/{slug}` (apex, **no** redirect)
- `location` = `City, Country/Region`
- `lastBuildDate`, `expectedJobCount`, `publisherUrl`

Do **not** add this URL to Google `Sitemap:` in robots (it is not a sitemap). Give it to BD. Document the known `applyUrl` “must start with https://www” quirk vs apex canonical.

Ops email to `LL-BD@linkedin.com`: daily listing count, markets (UK/DE/NL/PT/IE), search URL `https://kuchup.com/jobs`, sample `/jobs/<slug>` URLs, feed URL. Document this in [`docs/operations/seo-indexing.md`](docs/operations/seo-indexing.md) and [`docs/reference/job-syndication.md`](docs/reference/job-syndication.md).

## Tests

Extend [`tests/web/test_job_pages.py`](tests/web/test_job_pages.py):

- `GET /jobs` 200, contains `/jobs/{slug}` for a seeded visa role, `noindex` absent
- `?country=` filters; unknown country still 200 with empty/other groups
- Closed / non-visa roles omitted
- `GET /feeds/linkedin-jobs.xml` is `<source>` XML with `partnerJobId`, `applyUrl`, no closed rows
- `/sitemap.xml` lists `/jobs`; `/sitemap-jobs.xml` still slug-only

## Out of scope

- LinkedIn Job Posting API client
- Paying for Recruiter slots for the full catalog
- Changing Apply to the employer ATS
- Google Indexing API (does not notify LinkedIn)
